# Cues {#sec-cues}

::: {.callout-note}
## Stub — planned work
This chapter is not yet run. It is scoped here so the plan is on record.
:::

The decomposition of @sec-bootstrapping relocates the prize. The old social-cue work
(@sec-social) aimed accessible cues — prosody, discourse, pose — at *filtering frames*, and
found little. But filtering is the small rung (~+6, and region-MIL already takes most of it).
The large, open headroom is in the **referent label** (~+19), which splits into *word selection*
(+4.7, recoverable from speech ~63% of the time) and *vision-binding* (+8.1, the referent when it
isn't spoken at all).

So this chapter re-aims cues at **referent identification**, not frame selection:

- **Word selection (speech-side).** When the referent *is* spoken, which word is it? Test whether
  prosodic stress, discourse newness/topicality, and the concrete-noun bias can up-weight the
  referent word inside the utterance — approaching the "referent-where-spoken" oracle (73.2).
  Prior evidence is weak (cue↔Gemini ρ ≈ 0.14 for discourse, less for prosody), so expectations
  are tempered; the question is how much of the +4.7 is reachable.
- **Vision-binding (vision/social-side).** When the referent is *not* spoken, which visible object
  is being referred to? This is the larger prize (+8.1) and the harder problem — a
  gaze/hands/salience question, exactly what the pose and social cues should target, now measured
  against the referent oracle rather than CLIP alignment.

Success is measured as the fraction of each oracle rung an accessible-cue mechanism recovers, on
Konkle, tuned on the dev categories and reported on the Vong-60 (@sec-pipeline), with error bars.
